md_docs_2sync-tui(3) Library Functions Manual md_docs_2sync-tui(3)

NAME

md_docs_2sync-tui - Sync primitive inspector

In a debug build, press 0 during a session to open the live inspector. Press 0 or Escape to return to ASCII art. The 0 inspector, ? keyboard help, ] logs and o media input replace each other. Switching directly between them does not expose a media frame, and closing one never restores an older TUI. In the media editor these keys switch screens; paste paths or URLs containing shortcut characters to insert them as text.

  • Up/Down select the previous/next object, crossing page boundaries.
  • Left/Right move one page, preserving the row where possible and clamping at the endpoints. They preserve the selection when there is no previous/next page.
  • Home selects the first object on the first page, even from another row on that page.
  • End selects the last object on the last page. Repeated Home/End presses stay at the endpoint.
  • Resizing recalculates pages around the selected object.

The header reports the total objects, current page, selected item, sample age, and counts by type: M (mutex), RW (rwlock), C (condition variable), and A (integral/boolean/pointer atomic). The footer shows the selected object's registration location, address, owner/waiter, value, and last-operation age. Blue separators use UTF-8 line characters when UTF-8 is enabled and supported, or ASCII hyphens otherwise. Colors follow the configured log palette and --color-mode none disables them.

The list contains every live synchronization object in the named registry, including idle objects. It grows dynamically and is paginated; terminal height does not truncate the inventory. Mirror normally has fewer objects than a connected client because it does not create the connection's workers, transport, queues, and authentication state. File playback, audio, and active UI screens also affect the count. Destroyed objects are removed. When an initializer and its owner both register a primitive, the inspector counts that address once and displays its latest registration name. Child names include a registration ID so multiple audio buffers remain distinguishable.

This is a registry of instrumented ascii-chat primitives, not a scan of process memory. Raw C11 atomics, synchronization inside third-party libraries, and unregistered implementation bookkeeping do not automatically become entries. Embedded condition/rwlock counters are displayed in their parent object's state. New atomic_t/atomic_ptr_t session fields need explicit registration and unregistration before their storage is released. Register process-lifetime atomics after the named registry has initialized. Mutex/condition/rwlock initializers register their wrappers automatically. Audio and generic ring buffers register their atomic fields during creation and remove them on destruction.

Run the native regressions and live-mode checks with:

cmake --build build --target ascii-chat test-sync-regressions
uv run --project tests/ascii_chat_tests --frozen python -m pytest tests/python/integration/sync --sync-probe build/bin/test-sync-regressions.exe
python tests/integration/sync_tui_modes.py --binary build/bin/ascii-chat.exe --artifacts build/sync-tui-evidence
python tests/integration/tui_switching.py --binary build/bin/ascii-chat.exe

The live-mode test uses generated video/audio and loopback services. Its optional PNG exports render the captured PTY cells, alongside the exact ANSI stream and plain text; they do not require access to the user's terminal or webcam.

Version 0.14.7 ascii-chat
